login.title: Sign in
login.description: Enter your credentials to access Syncle.

setup.title: Create the admin account
setup.description: This is the first run. The account you create here is the single operator that protects every Syncle endpoint.
setup.usernameTooShort: Username must be at least 3 characters.
setup.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
setup.tokenHint: Printed in the server logs when Syncle starts — it proves you operate this server.
setup.tokenMissing: Enter the setup token from the server logs.
setup.tokenAuto: Verified as this server's operator — the setup token came from the machine running Syncle.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Credentials are encrypted at rest. Nothing leaves your machine.
connections.sshTunnelHint: Reach the database through an SSH jump host.
connections.sshPrivateKeyHint: Paste the PEM-encoded key (e.g. the contents of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519).
connections.tlsVerifyFull: Verify the authority and the host name (recommended)
connections.tlsDisableHint: Everything, including the password, crosses the network in plain text.
connections.tlsRequireHint: Stops passive eavesdropping only. The server’s certificate is not checked, so anyone able to sit between Syncle and the database can impersonate it.
connections.tlsVerifyCaHint: The certificate must come from a trusted authority, but any name on it is accepted — another server holding a certificate from the same authority would pass.
connections.tlsVerifyFullHint: The certificate must come from a trusted authority and be issued for this host. The only mode that proves you reached the right server.
connections.tlsCaHint: PEM. Leave empty to trust the system’s certificate authorities — the right choice for a managed database with a public certificate, not for a private CA.
connections.tlsServernameHint: Only if the certificate was issued for a different name than the host above (an IP address in the host field, for instance). Defaults to the host.
connections.tlsClientCertHint: PEM. Only for servers that require mutual TLS.
connections.tlsClientKeyHint: PEM. Encrypted at rest and never shown again.
connections.sshHostKeyHint: SHA256:… as `ssh-keygen -lf` prints it. Leave empty to record the key on first connection; after that a different key is refused.
connections.sshHostKeySeen: The SSH host presented {fingerprint}. It will be saved with this connection and checked from now on.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.deleteConfirmDescription: "{name}" and all of its connections and bridges will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.

bridges.selectJob: Select a job to see its delivery log.
bridges.positionLostTitle: This bridge cannot resume where it stopped
bridges.positionLostDescription: Continuing from now starts the bridge at the source's current position. Whatever changed at the source in between is not captured — run a replay afterwards to bring the destination up to date.
bridges.deleteDescription: This removes the bridge and its job history. This cannot be undone.

bridgeList.noBridges: No bridges in this workspace yet.

workspaceMap.noBridges: No bridges in this workspace yet
workspaceMap.description: A bridge moves data from a database to an endpoint.

bridgeBuilder.sendsAll: sends {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} · {cols}/{total} columns
bridgeBuilder.sendsSelected: sends {count, plural, one {# selected row} other {# selected rows}} · {cols}/{total} columns
bridgeBuilder.liveBannerRest: New rows added to this table will be delivered automatically — no row selection needed. Click a column header to include or exclude it from the payload.
bridgeBuilder.pickLive: Pick a connection and table to preview data and select columns.
bridgeBuilder.pickOneTime: Pick a connection and table to choose the data to send.
bridgeBuilder.oneTimeDesc: A one-time job: streams the rows once when you run it — good for backfills.
bridgeBuilder.liveDesc: A live bridge: listens and delivers changes the moment they happen.
bridgeBuilder.truncateHint: Off: when the source table is truncated the destination keeps its rows, and the timeline says so. On: the destination table is emptied too.
bridgeBuilder.cdcDesc: Streams changes from the DB log in real time (no polling).
bridgeBuilder.cdcReady: ✓ Ready — we’ll auto-create the publication & slot on start.
bridgeBuilder.watchDesc: The bridge keeps polling this table and delivers new rows as they appear.
bridgeBuilder.previewHint: Select a table and include at least one column to preview.
bridgeBuilder.dbDescPre: Write each row into one or more databases.
bridgeBuilder.dbDescPost: keeps targets in sync with no duplicates, even on replays. Cross-engine is supported (e.g. Postgres → MySQL or MongoDB).
bridgeBuilder.loadFailed: Could not load bridge for editing
bridgeBuilder.setAsideContinue: Set failed rows aside & keep syncing
bridgeBuilder.onFailureContinueHint: Rows that fail are kept in the bridge's dead-letter queue, in full, and can be retried once the cause is fixed. The bridge still stops if the destination itself is unavailable.
bridgeBuilder.onFailureStopHint: The bridge stops at the first failure without moving past it. Start it again and the same rows are retried; nothing is skipped.

deadLetters.waiting: {count, plural, one {# row waiting in the dead-letter queue} other {# rows waiting in the dead-letter queue}}
deadLetters.explainer: Could not be delivered, so they were set aside instead of lost.
deadLetters.entryMeta: {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} · delivery #{sequence} · {attempts, plural, =0 {not retried yet} one {# retry} other {# retries}}
deadLetters.moreNotShown: {count, plural, one {# more entry not shown} other {# more entries not shown}}
deadLetters.retryResolved: {count, plural, one {# entry delivered} other {# entries delivered}}
deadLetters.retryStillFailing: {count, plural, one {# entry is still failing} other {# entries are still failing}}
deadLetters.retryNeedsForce: {count, plural, one {# entry needs a decision: its source row is gone} other {# entries need a decision: their source rows are gone}}
deadLetters.discardDescription: {count, plural, one {# entry will never be delivered. The row stays on record, but this cannot be undone.} other {# entries will never be delivered. The rows stay on record, but this cannot be undone.}}
deadLetters.discarded: {count, plural, one {# entry discarded} other {# entries discarded}}
